summary: Michel Strickmann (1942–1994) worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Leiden, the EPHE, and Paris Diderot, and held positions at UC Berkeley (1978), the Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (1983–1985), and the University of Bordeaux (~1989–1994).

Michela Clemente is a Tibetologist who studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and conducted postdoctoral research under Hildegard Diemberger (2013–2015). She held a post as a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker (1835–1914) was an Italian scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Turin (~1853–1857) and taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and the University of Naples Federico II (~1872–1914).
Michele Martin (born 1942) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held an academic appointment at National Taiwan University.

Michelle Spuler (born 1971) specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Queensland (~1997–2001) and taught at Victoria University of Wellington (~2001–2003) and Colorado College.

Michiel de Vaan (born 1973) is a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his doctorate under Alexander Lubotsky (~1997–2002) and held a post at Leiden University from ~2002 to 2014.

Michihiko Komine (born 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University. He served as an assistant (attested 1978–1980) and professor (attested 2014–2015) at Taisho University, as well as a professor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

Michihiko Yajima (born 1958) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, where he was also affiliated in 1992, and later served as a professor at Tsurumi Women's University (attested 2003).

Michihiro Ikeda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He taught at Setagaya Gakuen High School (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), and served as a librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005–2006).

Michiko Yusa (born 1951) specializes in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She completed her doctoral studies under Raimon Panikkar at UC Santa Barbara (~1977–1983) and became a professor at Western Washington University around 1983.

Michio Kamikawa (1960–2021) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University (~1979–1988) and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University from ~1998 to 2021.

Michio Yano (born 1944) works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University and Brown University, working with Kiyoshi Yabuuchi and David Pingree, and was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from 1973 to 2015.

Michitoshi Barada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi. He held appointments at Otani University (attested 1992) and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2000–2026).
Michiya Ito was a graduate student and scholar affiliated with Tohoku University, holding posts attested there in 1990 and between 2001 and 2004.
Michiyo Hoshi (born 1941) is a researcher in Tibetology and linguistics. She has held posts at the Research Institute for Languages and Cultures of Asia and Africa and at Toyo Bunko (attested 2003).
Midori Nishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She undertook doctoral studies at Taisho University (attested 2006) and later worked there as a researcher (attested 2010–2015).
Mieko Kajihara is a scholar of Indology who studied under Michael Witzel at Harvard University, where she completed her PhD by 2002.

Migmar Tsering (1956–1999) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Khenpo Appey Rinpoche. He served as head of Sakya College (attested 1991–2003) and held posts at CIHTS and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Miguel de Unamuno (1864–1936) was a Spanish philosopher. He studied at Universidad Central from ~1880 to 1884 and held a faculty post at the University of Salamanca from ~1891 until 1936.

Mihai Eminescu (1850–1889) studied Indology and other subjects. He attended Staatsgymnasium Czernowitz, the University of Vienna (1869–1872), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1872–1874), where he was taught by Albrecht Weber.
